arun: Quick brainstorm: instead of a token bucket, what about exposing a compact runtime signal called 'supply_curve(tenant, region)' that expresses available capacity as a 0..1 float and a slope hint. Use case: let policy pick cheaper routes only when slope > threshold, otherwise prefer latency tiers.

priya: Interesting. Slope helps decide whether to steer traffic gradually. How would slope be computed? moving-average of consumption delta?

sam: Simple approach: two values per window: remaining_fraction and recent_drop_rate. remaining_fraction = tokens_left / window_capacity, drop_rate = (prev_window - curr_window)/window_capacity. Slope = clip(drop_rate, -1..1).

kate: Where to live? sidecar scorer, or central service that ingress caches per-tenant? Sidecar easier to iterate. Central helps global visibility for dedicated clusters.

arun: Sidecar is my vote: unix socket, tiny JSON responses. Ingress caches for 1s. Policy runtime reads header metadata. If missing, default to permissive and emit alert.

priya: DSL idea: builtin fn supply_curve(tenant, region) -> {"f":float, "s":float} but since payload must be simple, maybe two separate builtins: supply_fraction() and supply_slope(). Keep compiler happy: must be runtime hooks, not folded.

sam: Tests: ensure compiler treats both as non-deterministic runtime primitives. Add e2e measuring p99 impact w/ sidecar. Perf guard: header lookup + parse <1ms median.

kate: Telemetry: heatmap of fraction vs slope, rule flips, and number of decisions that changed route because slope indicated imminent drop. Dashboard tile for tenants with slope>0.2 over 3 windows.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: starting staging rollout for feature/supply-curve -> arch-staging (2 hosts) :rocket:

arun: Migration plan: opt-in per-tenant, shadow mode for 2w, canary enforcement for small set, full rollout. Runbook flag to disable enforcement instantly.

priya: Edge cases: cross-region requests should include both region scores; policy can choose min fraction, or combine slopes. Document recommended merge rules.

sam: Security: sign headers, don't trust client-supplied values. Sidecar must authenticate with central scorer if used.

kate: I'll sketch RFC with API, example DSL snippets, and telemetry mockups. Sam will prototype sidecar. Arun will write compiler guard tests.

arun: Thanks. We'll reconvene after RFC PR.
